task_description: This setup features a cart that moves along a straight track with a rigid rod hinged to it, free to swing about the attachment point. By applying horizontal forces to drive the cart left or right, the objective is to keep the rod upright and balanced above the moving base.
state_description:
The state is a vector of 4 elements, representing the following:
- state[0] The horizontal position of the base element (-inf to inf m)
- state[1] The angular displacement of the attached rotating element from the upright position
- state[2] The linear velocity of the base (-inf to inf rad)
- state[3] The angular velocity of the rotating element (-inf to inf rad)

The action space consists of a single bounded continuous control input representing the horizontal force applied to the base- action[0] Torque applied on the thigh rotor (-1 to 1 N)

The policy is a linear policy with 5 parameters and works as follows: 
action = argmax(state @ W + b), where
state = [cart_position, pole_angle, cart_velocity, pole_angular_velocity]
W = [[params[0]],
 [params[1]],
 [params[2]],
 [params[3]]]
b = [params[4]], where b is the bias term.
goal_description: Keeping the system upright and centered for as long as possible, preventing deviation or collapse while maintaining controlled motion.
